title: "Analysis code for the field study"
subtitle: "Homeostatic regulation of energetic arousal during acute social isolation- evidence from the lab and the field"
output:
  html_document:
    df_print: paged
---


```{r}

rm(list=ls())

library(readxl)
library(mousetrap)
library(dplyr)
library(misty)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(interactions)


# setwd("my path")

dat <- read_excel("field_data_2022-03-07.xlsx")

# Present data is a subset of a dataset collected in a larger EMA project investigating the effects of the COVID-19 lockdown on behaviour and wellbeing (Feneberg et al., 2022). For details on data selection, see data analysis preregistration  https://osf.io/6ynt3/.


```

# Outline and center variables

```{r}
# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
# Grouping and independent variables ---

# subject number of each participant
dat$ID <- as.factor(dat$ID)

# Condition (in manuscript - "type of day") - "Baseline" is a reference category compared to "Isolation"
# for details on how type of day was defined, see data analysis preregistration https://osf.io/6ynt3/
# express the conditions numerically before participant mean centering (PMC)
dat$cond_num[dat$Condition=="Baseline"] <- 0
dat$cond_num[dat$Condition=="Isolation"] <- 1

# Free time - whether the participants was engaged in free time (=1) or not (=0; e.g. work/study) 
# "What were you doing just before this assessment?". Participants could select one of either: working, studying, free time, or other
# express the conditions numerically before participant mean centering (PMC)
dat$freetime <- as.numeric(dat$freetime)

# Living condition - with others (=1), alone (=0)
dat$Living_cond <- as.numeric(dat$Living_cond)

# Sociability - subscale from the Social Reward Questionnaire (SRQ; Foulkes et al., 2014)
# score was created as a mean value from items 4, 10 and 15 (scale range [3-21]) 
dat$SRQ_sociability <- as.numeric(dat$SRQ_sociability)

# Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10; Klein et al., 2016)
# score was created as a sum value of all scale items (self-efficiency items were reverse-coded)
dat$PSS_chronic_stress <- as.numeric(dat$PSS_chronic_stress)

# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
# Dependent variables: psychological momentary measures ---

# Loneliness: "In the moment I feel... lonely", VAS 0-100 
dat$loneliness_VAS <- as.numeric(dat$loneliness_VAS)

# Desire for social contact: "How strong is your momentary desire for social exchange?", VAS 0-100
dat$desire_soc_VAS <- as.numeric(dat$desire_soc_VAS)

# Stress: "In the moment I feel... stressed", VAS 0-100
dat$stress_VAS <- as.numeric(dat$stress_VAS)

# Multidimensional mood questionnaire (MDBF) (Wilhelm & Schoebi, 2007)
# Each mood score was created as a mean of two items (see Wilhelm & Schoebi, 2007). Original scale was modified so that items were responded on visual analogue scales (0-100)

# MDBF, mood valence
dat$MDBF_valence_mood <- as.numeric(dat$MDBF_valence_mood)

# MDBF, calmness
dat$MDBF_calmness_mood <- as.numeric(dat$MDBF_calmness_mood)

# MDBF, energetic arousal 
dat$MDBF_energy_mood <- as.numeric(dat$MDBF_energy_mood)

# Fatigue: "In the moment I feel... exhausted", VAS 0-100
dat$fatigue_VAS <- as.numeric(dat$fatigue_VAS)

# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
# Other variables

# number of social interactions participant engaged in since the previous prompt
# "Have you had an uninterrupted social exchange of more than 2 minutes since the last entry/since getting up?" Participants answered yes/no and specified a number.
dat$soc_int_num <- as.numeric(dat$soc_int_num)


```

# Variable centering

```{r}
# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
# Participant mean centering (PMC) - level 1 variables

# Condition
dat <- scale_within(dat, variables="cond_num",  within="ID",prefix = "pmc_", center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)

# Freetime
dat <- scale_within(dat, variables="freetime",  within="ID",prefix = "pmc_", center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)

# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
# Grand mean centering (GMC) - level 2 variables

# Living condition
dat$gmc_Living_cond <- center(dat$Living_cond, type=c("CGM"))

# Sociability
dat$gmc_SRQ_sociability <- center(dat$SRQ_sociability, type=c("CGM"))

# Chronic stress
dat$gmc_PSS_chronic_stress <- center(dat$PSS_chronic_stress, type=c("CGM"))

```
# Alternative: standardizing outcomes
for easier comparison of effect sized (reported in Supplementary table 1)

# Run models

## 1. Loneliness

### Main effect of condition

```{r }

mod.loneliness.1 <- lmer(loneliness_VAS ~ pmc_cond_num +  ema_time  + pmc_freetime +
             (pmc_cond_num +  ema_time  + pmc_freetime  | ID), data = dat, 
           REML = TRUE, control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=2e5)))

summary(mod.loneliness.1)

```
### Interaction between condition and time

```{r}

mod.loneliness.2 <- lmer(loneliness_VAS ~ pmc_cond_num *  ema_time  + pmc_freetime +
             (pmc_cond_num *  ema_time  + pmc_freetime | ID), data = dat, 
           REML = TRUE, control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=2e5)))

summary(mod.loneliness.2)

# this model converges only when loneliness_VAS is not standardized; for consistency, the structure of the model was kept the same when reporting both raw and standardized beta coefficient.

```
### Interaction between condition and person-related characteristics

```{r}

mod.loneliness.3 <- lmer(loneliness_VAS ~ pmc_cond_num *  gmc_SRQ_sociability +
             pmc_cond_num* gmc_Living_cond +
             pmc_cond_num * gmc_PSS_chronic_stress+
             ema_time + pmc_freetime +
             ( pmc_cond_num +  ema_time  + pmc_freetime | ID), data = dat, 
           REML = TRUE, control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=2e5)))

summary(mod.loneliness.3)

# simple slope analysis of interaction between condition and living condition
sim_slopes(mod.loneliness.3, pred = pmc_cond_num, modx = gmc_Living_cond, cond.int = FALSE)

```


## 2. Desire for social contact

## 4. MDBF, mood valence

_Model comparison_
When complexity of model was reduced due to model with all random effects (pmc_cond_num +  ema_time + pmc_freetime |ID) was not converging, complexity of models was reduced. Sometimes two equally complex models were converging ((pmc_cond_num +  ema_time|ID) and  (ema_time + pmc_freetime |ID)). In these cases, the one with lower AIC criterion was chosen.

```{r}

m0.1 <- lmer(MDBF_valence_mood ~ pmc_cond_num +  ema_time  + pmc_freetime +
             ( pmc_cond_num +  ema_time  | ID), data = dat, 
           REML = FALSE, control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=2e5)))

m0.2 <- lmer(MDBF_valence_mood ~ pmc_cond_num +  ema_time  + pmc_freetime +
             ( pmc_cond_num + pmc_freetime  | ID), data = dat, 
           REML = FALSE, control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=2e5)))

anova(m0.1, m0.2)

m2.1 <- lmer(MDBF_valence_mood ~ pmc_cond_num *  gmc_SRQ_sociability +
             pmc_cond_num* gmc_Living_cond +
             pmc_cond_num * gmc_PSS_chronic_stress+
             + ema_time + pmc_freetime +
             ( pmc_cond_num + ema_time  | ID), data = dat, 
           REML = FALSE, control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=2e5)))

m2.2 <- lmer(MDBF_valence_mood ~ pmc_cond_num *  gmc_SRQ_sociability +
             pmc_cond_num* gmc_Living_cond +
             pmc_cond_num * gmc_PSS_chronic_stress+
             ema_time + pmc_freetime +
             ( pmc_cond_num + pmc_freetime  | ID), data = dat, 
           REML = FALSE, control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=2e5)))

anova(m2.1, m2.2)

```

### Main effect of condition

```{r }

mod.valence_mood.1 <- lmer(MDBF_valence_mood ~ pmc_cond_num +  ema_time  + pmc_freetime +
             (pmc_cond_num + pmc_freetime | ID), data = dat, 
           REML = FALSE, control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=2e5)))

# Random effect structure of more complex models that did not converge:
#   (pmc_cond_num +  ema_time  + pmc_freetime | ID) boundary (singular) fit: see ?isSingular, Model failed to converge with 1 negative eigenvalue: -4.6e+01

summary(mod.valence_mood.1)

```

### Interaction between condition and time

```{r}

mod.valence_mood.2 <- lmer(MDBF_valence_mood ~ pmc_cond_num *  ema_time  + pmc_freetime +
             ( pmc_cond_num + ema_time  + pmc_freetime  | ID), data = dat, 
           REML = TRUE, control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=2e5)))

summary(mod.valence_mood.2)

# Random effect structure of more complex models that did not converge:
#   ( pmc_cond_num * ema_time  + pmc_freetime  | ID) boundary (singular) fit: see ?isSingular

```

### Interaction between condition and person-related characteristics

```{r}

mod.valence_mood.3 <- lmer(MDBF_valence_mood ~ pmc_cond_num *  gmc_SRQ_sociability +
             pmc_cond_num* gmc_Living_cond +
             pmc_cond_num * gmc_PSS_chronic_stress +
             ema_time + pmc_freetime +
             ( pmc_cond_num + pmc_freetime | ID), data = dat, 
           REML = TRUE, control=lmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa", optCtrl=list(maxfun=2e5)))

# Random effect structure of more complex models that did not converge:
#   ( pmc_cond_num * ema_time  + pmc_freetime  | ID) boundary (singular) fit: see ?isSingular
#   ( pmc_cond_num + ema_time  + pmc_freetime  | ID) boundary (singular) fit: see ?isSingular, Model failed to converge with 1 negative eigenvalue: -5.4e+02

summary(mod.valence_mood.3)

```
